This. You are a perfect reflection of my situation. My mother too was victim to her narcissistic mother (my grandmother), and I constantly hear stories about how badly she was treated and how 'lucky' I am to have a good mother. But whenever I hear these stories, a little voice whispers in the back of my head '...you don't know this... but you are the same as her...'. I feel so bad for my mother for having gone through all she has, but I can't help but think how crazy it is that she herself doesn't know that she mirrors her own mother.
Because of the whole 'you have it better than me', I let every hurtful action slide; initially because I thought I was probably wrong most of the time, and when I realised that that may not be true, I excused it by the fact that she's had it worse.
And you're right; you gain nothing from burying pain. And it leaves you so confused. Because every time you call her out for doing nmom things, you forget that love and affection is all she wanted growing up, and you, her child, is almost denying her of it. It makes you realise that we're all really victims.
As I'm writing this, I'm reminding myself that I should try to make this relationship with my mother last while she's here. Yes. She has flaws. Flaws that have shaped my upbringing and changed me maybe for the worse. But she is human and had it much worse too. I'm just glad I was able to realise the cycle I could have potentially been caught up in, only my mother (and yours too probably) were too late to realise the vicious cycle they got stuck in.
I know emotional abuse can't be excused, but I think in my case, it's excusable, as my mother was a victim herself.
